package_info.package_name: SolarWinds Orion (SunBurst), 3CX Desktop App, Progress MOVEit
package_info.package_versions: Impacted versions at time of attack (e.g., Orion Platform 2019.4 HF 5 through 2020.2.1 HF 1, 3CX Desktop App v18.12.407 & v18.12.416, MOVEit Transfer 2023.0.0, etc.)
package_info.why_malicious: These commercial software packages were compromised by attackers who inserted malicious code or backdoors into trusted software updates or binaries, enabling widespread malware distribution to enterprise and government customers. The attacks leveraged the trust and reputation of the vendors to bypass traditional security controls and deliver malware at scale.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime after update, the code checks for specific conditions, collects system and environment information, and exfiltrates it to a hardcoded attacker-controlled domain, enabling remote access and further compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is hidden within a trusted signed update, performs stealthy system reconnaissance, and communicates with an external C2 domain.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal update code should not perform covert data collection or external network communication to unknown domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Telemetry or update checks to vendor domains (but not to attacker infrastructure).

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code downloads a remote icon file, extracts an embedded payload, and executes it, enabling arbitrary code execution and further malware delivery.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code fetches a remote resource from a suspicious domain, extracts and executes hidden code, which is a classic malware loader pattern.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate desktop apps should not download and execute code from untrusted external sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Auto-updaters or plugin systems (with strict validation and trusted sources).

execution_context.file_location: MOVEit Transfer web application (DLL or script file)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code responds to crafted requests by executing arbitrary SQL commands and exfiltrating database contents to an attacker-controlled domain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code enables remote attackers to execute arbitrary database commands and exfiltrate sensitive data, indicating a deliberate backdoor or severe vulnerability.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Web applications should validate input and never allow arbitrary SQL execution or data exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: Attacker compromises vendor build or update infrastructure and inserts malicious code into a trusted software update or binary.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is distributed to customers via normal update channels.

attack_chain.action: Customers install or update the compromised software, triggering execution of the malicious code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code runs with trusted permissions inside enterprise networks.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code performs reconnaissance, downloads additional payloads, or exfiltrates sensitive data to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains persistent access, can move laterally, or steal data.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected network connections from trusted software to non-vendor domains
Execution of code or payloads downloaded at runtime
Unusual system or environment data collection by update processes
SQL injection or arbitrary command execution triggered by crafted requests
file_indicators: Modified or unsigned DLLs/binaries in vendor software directories
Presence of unexpected scripts or loader files
Unusual changes to application update files
network_indicators: Connections to known C2 domains (e.g., avsvmcloud.com, iconstorage.com, attacker.com)
Outbound data transfers to non-vendor IPs/domains after software updates
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unexpected network activity from commercial software, especially connections to non-vendor domains. Use file integrity monitoring to detect unauthorized changes to binaries or update files. Analyze process behavior for signs of code injection, payload downloads, or abnormal data collection. Employ EDR/XDR solutions to correlate suspicious activity with known supply chain attack patterns.
